title: The Beach
statementMd:
Andrew loves the sea. That's why, at the height of the summer season, he decided to go to the beach, taking a sunbed with him to sunbathe.

The beach is a rectangular field with $n$ rows and $m$ columns. Some cells of the beach are free, some have roads, stones, shops and other non-movable objects. Some of two adjacent along the side cells can have sunbeds located either horizontally or vertically.

Andrew hopes to put his sunbed somewhere, but that's a bad luck, there may no longer be free places for him! That's why Andrew asked you to help him to find a free place for his sunbed. Andrew's sunbed also should be places on two adjacent cells.

If there are no two adjacent free cells, then in order to free some place for a sunbed, you will have to disturb other tourists. You can do the following actions:

- Come to some sunbed and, after causing $p$ units of discomfort to its owner, lift the sunbed by one of its sides and rotate it by $90$ degrees. One half of the sunbed must remain in the same cell and another half of the sunbed must move to the free cell. At the same time, anything could be on the way of a sunbed during the rotation . ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/0b99c9c60a4e51d48facd8ce267ea733afdd57c0.png)![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7a26b58202306eeab15d960ba1e13c0d736aa30b.png)![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/cf1ccd3d9ea43c21a6c7d044e0e11c9fccdf993d.png) Rotation of the sunbed by $90$ degrees around cell $(1, 2)$.
- Come to some sunbed and, after causing $q$ units of discomfort to its owner, shift the sunbed along its long side by one cell. One half of the sunbed must move to the place of another, and another — to the free cell. ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/0b99c9c60a4e51d48facd8ce267ea733afdd57c0.png)![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7a26b58202306eeab15d960ba1e13c0d736aa30b.png)![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/2444008536a396e8a9e35557530527305a8d88c7.png) Shift of the sunbed by one cell to the right.

In any moment each sunbed occupies two adjacent free cells. You cannot move more than one sunbed at a time.

Help Andrew to free a space for his sunbed, causing the minimum possible number of units of discomfort to other tourists, or detect that it is impossible.

## Input

The first line contains two integers $n$ and $m$ ($1 \le n, m \le 300\,000$, $1 \le n \cdot m \le 300\,000$) — the number of rows and columns in rectangle.

The second line contains two integers $p$ and $q$ ($1 \le p, q \le 10^9$) — the number of units of discomfort caused by rotation and shift of a sunbed, respectively.

Each of the following $n$ lines contains $m$ characters, describing cells of the rectangle. Each lines consists of characters "`L`", "`R`", "`D`", "`U`", "`.`" and "`#`", denoting the type of the cell. Characters "`L`", "`R`", "`D`" and "`U`" denote a half of a sunbed placed in the cell — left, right, bottom and top half, respectively. Character "`.`" denotes a free cell and character "`#`" — a cell, occupied by some non-movable object.

## Output

Print one integer — the minimum possible number of units of discomfort, caused to other tourists, to free a space for a sunbed. If it is impossible to free a space for a sunbed, print $-1$.

## Note

In the first example we can shift upper sunbed to the left and lower sunbed — to the right. Andrew will be able to put his sunbed vertically in the middle of the beach. We well cause $2 + 2 = 4$ units of discomfort. It is easy to prove that it is an optimal answer.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ef8aec374ae9f1a4ab8bf4632a892ea366a15791.png)![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7a26b58202306eeab15d960ba1e13c0d736aa30b.png)![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a82f34c7c0e74583f2756088bba640f78dc48863.png) Optimal strategy in the first example (Andrew's sunbed is colored white).

In the second example it is impossible to free a space for Andrew's sunbed. All possible states of the beach after any rotates and shifts are illustrated in the problem statement.
statementZhMd:
安德鲁喜欢大海。因此，在盛夏时节，他决定带着一张躺椅去海滩晒太阳。

海滩是一个有 $n$ 行 $m$ 列的矩形区域。海滩上的一些格子是空闲的，另一些格子中有道路、石头、商店和其他不可移动的物体。部分共享边的相邻格子中放置着躺椅，躺椅可以横放或竖放。

安德鲁希望找个地方放下自己的躺椅，但运气不太好：可能已经没有空闲位置了！因此，安德鲁请你帮他找到一个可以放置躺椅的空闲位置。安德鲁的躺椅也必须放在两个相邻的格子中。

如果不存在两个相邻的空闲格子，那么为了腾出放置躺椅的位置，你需要打扰其他游客。你可以执行以下操作：

- 来到某张躺椅旁，在给其所有者造成 $p$ 单位的不适后，抬起躺椅的一侧并将其旋转 $90$ 度。躺椅的一半必须留在原来的格子中，另一半必须移动到空闲格子中。在旋转过程中，躺椅经过的路径上可以有任何物体。 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/0b99c9c60a4e51d48facd8ce267ea733afdd57c0.png)![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7a26b58202306eeab15d960ba1e13c0d736aa30b.png)![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/cf1ccd3d9ea43c21a6c7d044e0e11c9fccdf993d.png) 绕格子 $(1, 2)$ 将躺椅旋转 $90$ 度。
- 来到某张躺椅旁，在给其所有者造成 $q$ 单位的不适后，沿躺椅的长边将其平移一个格子。躺椅的一半必须移动到另一半所在的位置，另一半则移动到空闲格子中。 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/0b99c9c60a4e51d48facd8ce267ea733afdd57c0.png)![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7a26b58202306eeab15d960ba1e13c0d736aa30b.png)![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/2444008536a396e8a9e35557530527305a8d88c7.png) 将躺椅向右平移一个格子。

在任何时刻，每张躺椅都占据两个相邻的空闲格子。你不能同时移动多于一张躺椅。

请帮助安德鲁腾出放置躺椅的空间，使对其他游客造成的不适总单位数尽可能少，或者判断这是不可能的。

## 输入格式

第一行包含两个整数 $n$ 和 $m$（$1 \le n, m \le 300\,000$，$1 \le n \cdot m \le 300\,000$），表示矩形区域的行数和列数。

第二行包含两个整数 $p$ 和 $q$（$1 \le p, q \le 10^9$），分别表示旋转和平移一张躺椅造成的不适单位数。

接下来的 $n$ 行中，每行包含 $m$ 个字符，描述矩形区域中的格子。每行由字符 `L`、`R`、`D`、`U`、`.` 和 `#` 组成，分别表示格子的类型。字符 `L`、`R`、`D` 和 `U` 表示躺椅的一半位于该格子中，分别代表左半、右半、下半和上半。字符 `.` 表示空闲格子，字符 `#` 表示被某个不可移动物体占据的格子。

## 输出格式

输出一个整数，即为腾出放置躺椅的空间时，对其他游客造成的不适单位数的最小可能值。如果无法腾出放置躺椅的空间，输出 $-1$。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，我们可以将上方的躺椅向左移动，将下方的躺椅向右移动。这样，安德鲁就可以在海滩中央竖直放置自己的躺椅。我们造成的不适为 $2 + 2 = 4$ 单位。很容易证明这是最优答案。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ef8aec374ae9f1a4ab8bf4632a892ea366a15791.png)![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7a26b58202306eeab15d960ba1e13c0d736aa30b.png)![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a82f34c7c0e74583f2756088bba640f78dc48863.png) 第一个样例中的最优策略（安德鲁的躺椅用白色表示）。

在第二个样例中，不可能为安德鲁腾出放置躺椅的空间。题面中展示了海滩经过任意旋转和平移后所有可能的状态。
